# Relativistic Quantum Mechanics

Content:

Quantum wavefunctions as a "classical" complex field
Einstein-Plank relation
de Broglie relation
4-vector formulation of these
Plane-wave to motivate Energy and Momentum operators

Construct Schrodinger equation and its essential properties. Mention spin has to be bolted on by hand. Not relativistic.

Include drop-down box for the Schrodinger Lagrangian and Noether current - state don't derive.

Motivate coupling to EM via the classical non-relativistic Lagrangian, leading to the covariant derivative for minimal coupling. Discuss gauge transformations and how a local phase transformation is required to make the covariant derivative "covariant".

Introduce the Klein-Gordon equation 
Discuss properties and plane-wave solutions (has been discussed earlier so can be a recap)
Focus on the complex Lagrangian (mention real one) and compute its Noether current. 
Discuss problems with the KG equation, negative probability density, negative energies.

Show KG equation is covariant.

Mention KG is not really minimally coupled (like Schrodinger)

Motivate the Dirac equation in its Schrodinger-like form - by introducing 4-spinors (a new object). Show how it can be written in a covariant form once we account for 4-spinors transforming under Lorentz transformations. Derive the Noether current.
Move to interacting Dirac equation and show it is minimally coupled. 

Arrive at the "classical" QED Lagrangian.
